# Āpāyika Sutta (Iti 48 (It 2.21 PTS It 42))

**ID:** Iti 48 (It 2.21 PTS It 42)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Āpāyika Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Āpāyika Sutta* ("Bound for Loss"; Iti 48; PTS It 42) is located in the *Dukanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka*. The text concerns two varieties of unwholesome behavior that doom an individual to rebirth in hell. A central element of the discourse's verses is the antithetical warning regarding monastic conduct and the receipt of alms: it is proclaimed better for an immoral, unrestrained practitioner to swallow a burning, red-hot iron ball than to consume the almsfood provided by the faithful [Marino 2017]. J. A. Marino notes that this striking image—serving as an inverted foil to the pious alms round (*piṇḍapāta*)—echoes early Indian depictions of hellish retribution against gluttonous monastics and reappears expanded within texts such as the *Aggikkhandhopama Sutta* [Marino 2017].

 Individual verses correspond to *Dhammapada* verses 306, 307, and 308, as well as verses in the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada*, the Patna *Dharmapada*, the *Udānavarga* (UV 8, 9, 11), the *Kokālika Sutta* (Snp 3.10), and the *Sundarī Sutta* (Ud 4.8). DharmaNexus records matching Pali-internal text reuse with *Dhammapada* 306–308, the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Jīvika Sutta* (Iti 91), the *Sattakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, and other *Itivuttaka* discourses (Iti 31, Iti 42, Iti 49) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the passage with the Tibetan *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīprātimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112) [DharmaNexus].
